cases.description: Valid section index but the internal section list is null; removeRecord should return false and not touch the header.
Section list exists but does not contain the supplied record; remove returns false, so removeRecord should return false and header.decCount must not be invoked.
Section list contains the record; remove succeeds, so removeRecord should return true and invoke header.decCount once for the given section.
Section index is out of the allowed range; Section.check should throw IllegalArgumentException, which propagates from removeRecord.
Section index exceeds the maximum allowed value; Section.check should throw IllegalArgumentException and the method must not touch any internal state.
The section list is non‑null but empty; remove returns false, so removeRecord should return false and header.decCount must not be invoked.
The section contains the same record twice; removeRecord should remove only the first occurrence, return true, and call header.decCount exactly once.
The section list contains a null entry and the caller passes null as the record; List.remove(null) succeeds, so removeRecord should return true and invoke header.decCount once.
The section is backed by an immutable list (e.g., Collections.emptyList()); attempting to remove a record throws UnsupportedOperationException, which should propagate out of removeRecord.
The internal `sections` array is null. After `Section.check` passes, the method attempts to access `sections[section]` which throws a NullPointerException.
The `header` field is null while the target section list contains the record. Removal succeeds, but the subsequent call to `header.decCount(section)` triggers a NullPointerException.
The header's count for the given section is already zero. After the record is removed, `header.decCount(section)` attempts to decrement below zero and throws IllegalArgumentException.

The `sections` array is deliberately created with a length smaller than the valid section index (e.g., length 2). `Section.check` passes, but accessing `sections[section]` results in an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
